Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Round End 4 Cards 5 Game End Overview Play units to three lanes in order to have the most power and thus gain control of the lane, control a lane twice or more in a row to deal damage to your opponent until they die Turn At the start of a round, draw 5 cards then you may discard a card to draw a replacement once Put your personal god into your hand, so you now have 6 cards After which, take alternating turns to play all 6 cards Upon playing a card, pick which lane you wish to assign it to, and generally speaking it will stay there for the rest of the round Each lane can only hold 2 of your cards If the card played has a Placement Ability, resolve it and apply its effects to whichever player you wish After all cards are placed, resolve each lane from lowest base value to highest base value Turn over each Stealth (facedown) card when its lane is being evaluated Resolve all Combat abilities of the lane simultaneously Whoever has the most power wins the lane, if it is not theirs then it becomes theirs, whilst if it was theirs already then the loser is dealt 1 damage (ties result in nothing happening) Round End Once all lanes are resolved, flip all the lane cards so the control remains the same All playing cards are discarded, and the gods are returned to their owners Cards The number at the central top of a card shows its power, this is sometimes a flat number but sometimes may be modified by the lane it is played in depicted by the matching symbol On the lower section of the card is an ability, these can either be a when played ability or a during combat ability On the upper sides of some cards, there may also appear a stealth symbol, these cards will be placed facedown when played Game End The game ends as soon as one player has 3 or more damage, as such all lanes may not be resolved that round The player who is still alive, wins! According the some sources, each sunrise and sunset mark the backdrop for the perpetual battle between Horus and Seth. In this never-ending combat, Seth, god of darkness and chaos, prevails over Horus with the arrival of each night. However, in an eternal cycle of revenge, the victory of Horus, god of the sky, heralds the coming of each new day, continuing a cycle which has endured since the beginning of time.

In the game, Horus and Seth face each other in three locations: the world of the living (the Deshret), the underworld (the Duat) and the Sun Boat, or Mandjet, which symbolises the sun’s journey across the sky.

Sunrise Sunset is a competitive game for two opponents where in each round players take turns in playing cards (up to a total of 6 each) in order to gain control of the three locations. In each location the opponent with more power takes control.

The first player to deal three damage is the victor of the game.

Beginning with the starting player, the players take turns to play cards one after another until they have played all of their cards  and assign it to one of the three lanes of your choice. The cards with stealth are played facedown, unlike the cards without stealth, which are played faceup.

If the card that you play has a placement ability, this is applied immediately.

Once each player has played all of their cards, determine who is the victor and loser in each lane. Apply all of the combat abilities of the units placed and add up the power of the cards which are placed in their area of the lane.

If a player deals 3 damage or more to their opponent at any moment, the game ends immediately.

—description from the publisher

[Rating: 3/10] Recht dreister Klon von Blue Moon, und dann auch noch mit weniger Lanes. Da reißt es auch das wunderschöne Artwork nicht mehr raus...

[Rating: 3/10] [b]Lane battler with lots of special powers[/b]  + Compact lineup of characters; I appreciate the restrained design + Draft in the beginning to cycle a character + Design cuts two ways: the unusual powers are intriguing to make go off  - Very unusual and challenging powers that always feel hard to use - Rounds are very fast without much back and forth - Powers are difficult to internalize and predict - I liked the old abstract theme more than buff pharaoh gods  Microgame that is reminiscent of a more complex Air, Land, & Sea without the good part. Very not for me.

[Rating: 4/10] Initial Impressions: I thought this would be like Hanamikoji, but the play felt too limited and obviously I'd play a card in this lane over another, except you try to stall because you don't know where your opponent is going to play some reversal cards. That is, the imperfect information feels pretty one dimensional.
